We recently hired Vows Vachan for our wedding, and unfortunately, their services were a complete letdown. While we expected a well-organized and seamless experience, what we got was chaos, mismanagement, and a complete lack of professionalism.

The negatives:
- Lack of execution & coordination: From the very beginning, there was no structured planning, leading to confusion at every stage. My sister and I barely got to participate in the wedding, as we were constantly solving problems, managing tasks, and searching for team members who were missing when needed.
- Unreliable team support: During both pujas, not a single team member was available, forcing us to handle everything on our own.
- Guest dissatisfaction: Many of our guests approached us, frustrated with the disorganization and lack of assistance, questioning why we had hired a team that seemed completely unhelpful.
- Disastrous departures: There was no structure in place for guest departures, and the team failed to manage hotel staff, leading to unnecessary confusion and frustration.
- False claims of experience: Despite assurances that they had extensive experience working in Goa, it was clear that this was not the case. The team failed to coordinate with local vendors and mismanaged transport services, making things even more inconvenient.
- Poor vendor management: The options provided for arrangements were subpar, rushed, and lacked any real thought or practicality. Even for the musical pheras, where we had already selected a vendor, the team failed to ensure smooth execution.
- Mediocre décor, not as per expectations: The décor was not what we had asked for—the proportions were wrong, and the excessive use of artificial flowers was disappointing.

Final verdict:
Working with Vows Vachan was a frustrating and stressful experience, and we do not recommend their services to anyone. Instead of handling logistics and ensuring a smooth wedding, they added to our stress and failed at every level of execution. This feedback is being shared with all heads of Vows Vachan, as this was not just a failure of one team but a complete breakdown in management. If you are considering them for your wedding, think twice before making the same mistake we did.
